gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the three headline figures it compared on one basis: the MINI 2's '0.02 mm' is single-frame precision and point distance (its accuracy is 0.05 mm), the Seal's '0.01 mm' is an accuracy figure with no test condition and a 0.05 mm resolution, and the Raptor's '0.02 mm' has no condition on any page I could open.
standout_why: Compared against cited 3dprinting.com small-format guide (already lists MINI 2 as 0.05 mm single-frame accuracy + 0.02 mm point precision, Seal 0.01 mm accuracy / 0.05 mm resolution, Seal Lite 0.02 / 0.07 mm), cited makermachinesatlas.com (MINI 2 0.05 mm accuracy, 0.02 mm point spacing; says point spacing alone does not prove accuracy) and cited comparefoundry.com (says Revopoint labels 0.02 mm as single-frame precision and point distance, defines precision as repeatability, and gives Moose accuracy with no condition). Cited print3dindex.com returned 403. Between them the rivals already split the MINI 2's numbers and list the Seal's raw numbers. None of them gives the Seal's 0.01 mm a test condition or puts the Raptor's 0.02 mm next to its mode or test distance. I could not source those missing pieces either, so a normalised table would mostly repeat what the rivals already say.
decides: On a like-for-like basis, ChatGPT's 'MINI 2 = 0.02 mm, best for fine detail' compares a point-distance and repeatability figure with the Seal's 0.05 mm resolution and the Raptor's accuracy figure. Comparing accuracy with accuracy, the MINI 2 states 0.05 mm, the Seal 0.01 mm (no condition) and the Seal Lite 0.02 mm. Comparing detail with detail, the MINI 2 states 0.02 mm point distance, the Seal 0.05 mm and the Seal Lite 0.07 mm. This supports our page's split: the MINI 2 for the finest detail (jewelry, 28 mm minis) and the Seal as the all-round pick. It does not settle Seal against Raptor on accuracy, because neither maker's test condition could be sourced.
